# SK2194 — The captured primary constructor parameter is assigned

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A member body of a class or struct with a primary constructor assigns one of its parameters, so the compiler-generated capture field is mutable instance state that appears in no declaration.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | 12.0 |
| Since | 2.0 |
| ReSharper | `CapturedPrimaryConstructorParameterIsMutable` (`resharper_captured_primary_constructor_parameter_is_mutable_highlighting`) |

## Why

Capture itself is the feature: a parameter read from a member body becomes a hidden field, and that is what primary constructors are for. What the language gives no way to say is that the field is `readonly`. The moment a body writes the parameter, the type carries mutable state with no declaration, no modifier, no name a reader can search for, and no visibility to any tool that reasons about fields — and the write reads as an assignment to a parameter, which is local by every habit a reader has.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
sealed class Retry(int attempts) {
    public bool Next() {
        attempts--;          // writes the hidden capture field
        return attempts > 0;
    }
}
```

Write:

```csharp
sealed class Retry(int attempts) {
    int remaining = attempts;

    public bool Next() {
        remaining--;
        return remaining > 0;
    }
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **Capture is not the finding and a read is never reported.** `PrimaryConstructorParameterCaptureDisallowed` — the second inspection on the originating issue, which the export ships at `none` — asks a project-policy question about whether captures are allowed at all, and that is a configuration choice rather than a defect. The finding here is the write. ⚠ **`CS9107` was probed and covers a different overlap, and it is not `CS9124`.** The compiler warns, always on and with no analyzer package, when a captured parameter's value is *also passed to the base constructor*, because the base may capture it too; it says nothing about a parameter that is merely assigned. A parameter named in the base-constructor argument list is excluded here rather than reported twice. ⚠ **Records are excluded, and the reason is the trap this repository has already paid for.** In a positional record the parameter is also where the property is written down, both symbols point at the same `ParameterSyntax`, and a name in a member body resolves to the property rather than to the capture — a different analysis with a different answer, and guessing at it from the parameter's shape is how a rule ships dead. The exclusion is structural: a record is a different syntax node, so the analyzer never sees one. ⚠ **A field or property initializer is not a member body.** Initializers run while the constructor is running, where the parameter is an ordinary parameter and writing it captures nothing; the same goes for the base-constructor argument list. Simple assignment, compound assignment, `++`/`--` and `ref`/`out` arguments all count as writes. Report-only: the repair is to declare the field the code is already using — a new declaration, a name for it and an edit at every use — and where the write was a mistake the repair is to delete it instead. Those move the type in opposite directions and the assignment does not say which was meant. Silent below C# 12, where the shape cannot exist.
